narrative: Your loan was denied because the model estimated a 42.0% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. That does not mean default is certain; it means the estimated risk was above the cutoff the bank uses for approval. The decision was shaped mainly by three factors. Your credit history was the single most influential factor and, in your case, it leaned toward good credit rather than driving the denial. The amount you requested—4,249 DM, above the approved average of about 3,020 DM—was the second most important factor and also leaned slightly toward good credit. The main factor pushing against you was your checking-account status: your balance is in the 0–200 DM range. Among approved applicants, no checking account is the most common profile, while a 0–200 DM balance appears in only about 18% of approvals, so this factor raised your risk score. The denial therefore came from the overall combination: the checking-account signal and other parts of your profile outweighed the favorable credit-history and loan-amount signals. To improve a future application, ask the bank for the specific reasons recorded on your file, correct any credit-history errors, work on maintaining a stronger checking and savings relationship, and consider a smaller or better-secured loan or adding a guarantor. You may also ask what conditions would make approval possible.
